analysis.title: Global Single-Stock Volatility Landscape - 29th October 2026
key_insights: UBS Derivatives Strategy suggests adding defensive exposure to the European AI ecosystem. Over the 18 months into late June, AI beneficiaries outperformed AI at-risk stocks by about 190% in the US and over 100% in Europe. Since then one third of the US outperformance has reversed, and more than half in Europe.

UBS Equity Strategy (Gerry Fowler) expects AI-monetisation risk premia to fade and suggests owning structural cycles (tech, industrials, materials, banks) over crowded US AI leaders. His 'AI Capex 2.0' note says earnings upgrades are moving down the chain and much of Tier 2 is European.

Bullish trade set for European AI names: buy ASML Mar27 call spreads, Schneider (SU FP) Dec26 call spreads, Air Liquide (AI FP) Dec26 call spreads, and Siemens Energy (ENR GY) and Anglo American (AAL LN) Dec26 call-spread collars.

ASML 19Mar27 EUR1800/2000 call spread costs EUR30 (2% indicative) vs EUR1492 spot, a 5.7x return on premium if the stock gets 55% of the way to the UBS target in 5 months. UBS Research says ASML's valuation leaves room for disappointment (a 50% cut to 2028 EPS on 22x implies EUR1400, -6%).

Schneider 18Dec26 EUR270/290 call spread costs EUR3.03 (1.2%) vs EUR245.7 spot, a 5.6x return if the stock recovers to early-October levels by year-end. Air Liquide 18Dec26 EUR182/188 call spread costs EUR1.31 (75bps) vs EUR174.02, a 3.6x return if the stock gets 54% of the way to the UBS target.

Siemens Energy 18Dec26 EUR160/180/100 call-spread collar costs EUR1.20 (90bps) vs EUR133.28 spot. Anglo American 18Dec26 4000/4400/3200p call-spread collar costs 66.4p (1.7%) vs 3804p spot. UBS Research ranks Siemens Energy first among preferred electrification/data-centre stocks after the sell-off.

The UBS screen of European AI-ecosystem names shows 2m ATMF implied vol highest at ENR GY (52.1%), ANTO LN (47.7%), ASM NA (46.6%) and PRY IM (44.6%). ASML is at 39.4% implied vol, with skew near the low end of its five-year range.

Put-selling trade: UBS Research sees China AI hardware as oversold, with valuations near historical troughs despite 12-15% earnings upgrades over three months and fast-money positioning unwound to start-of-year levels. Kevin Cheng highlights YOFC (6869 HK) and Kingboard Laminates (1888 HK), whose earnings cases rest on supply constraints.

YOFC and KBL 2m ATMF implied vols are 80-90 vol, in the top decile of three-year ranges, and shares are down 20-30% since October Golden Week (YOFC -33.7%, KBL -17.8% vs 9 Oct). UBS suggests selling put premium for yield.

Sell YOFC 30Dec26 $92.5 (88.5%) puts for $8.2 (7.9%), spot ref $104.5, -29 delta, 84 vol, breakeven $84.27 (80.6%). Sell KBL 30Dec26 $34 (88.7%) puts for $2.8 (7.4%), spot ref $38.34, -30 delta, 78 vol, breakeven $31.18 (81.3%).

Largest weekly spot moves: US: BA -13.1%, CRWD +11.4%, LULU +9.0%, TXN +8.8%, GM +8.4%. Europe: KER FP -18.3%, FR FP -15.2%, SAF FP -13.4%, ADYEN NA -13.0%, SAN SQ -11.1%. APAC: 005930 KP +8.3%, 992 HK -8.5%, 2018 HK +7.1%, 5 HK -7.0%, 2269 HK -6.2%.

Index implied vols: SPX 3m IV 14.8% (spot 96th percentile over 2 years), NDX 21.3%, RTY 19.1%, SX5E 17.0%, DAX 17.0%, SMI 13.8%, UKX 13.1%. Europe's 3m rich (IV minus realised) is +5.3 vol for SX5E and +4.5 for SPX.

US listed-options activity 22-28 Oct was led by Micron ($98.95bn 1w ADN, 1.9x its 1y average, 58% calls) and Tesla ($92.51bn, 0.9x). NVDA was $47.70bn (0.8x), AAPL $38.81bn (1.2x) and AMD $32.21bn (1.6x). Most elevated vs history: NSC and WMB (3.5x, ~93-95% calls), PG 2.4x, STX 2.2x, GE 2.1x, FSLR 2.1x.

European options activity was highest in ASML ($566.9m, 0.7x its 1y average), Novartis (1.6x), Siemens Energy (1.4x) and Eni (2.7x). Most elevated vs history: BT 5.0x (100% calls), Campari 3.8x, Pearson 3.5x, Evonik 3.4x (3% calls), Santander 3.2x (20% calls).
APAC options activity was led by Alibaba ($770.6m, 0.9x) and Tencent ($751.1m, 0.8x). Elevated vs history: Keyence 4.1x, Sinopharm 2.3x, Lenovo 2.3x, Nongfu 2.3x, NetEase 2.0x.

Option-selling screens after large declines (low RSI, high percentile IV): Europe SAF, KER, CA, SAN, HSBA, FR, ADYEN; US SE (64% IV), BA, TAL, WB, NFLX, BKNG, WYNN, BABA. Call-overwriting candidates on strength: Europe ROP (Roche), PHIA, IMB, HEIA; US LMT (+14.2% in 5d), PD, UPS, TXN.

Option-buying screens (lowest IV percentile vs history): Europe BOSS GY (9.8% IV, 0th percentile), DHER, AV/, AGN, PSON; US WB, PDD, UBER, TSLA, NSC, NFLX, JD; APAC 788 HK, 9868 HK, 6618 HK, 2020 HK, 9618 HK.
Dual-listing screen compares implied vol across listings, for example NOK US implied spread 78.9% vs 55.8% for NOKIA FH on 1m, and ERIC US 47.5% vs ERICB SS 35.0%.

market_movers.rationale: Derivatives desk suggests Mar27 call spreads. UBS target is +62% vs the 2m screen spot, but UBS Research cautions valuation leaves room for disappointment.
Siemens Energy (ENR GY) Dec26 call-spread collar. UBS Research ranks it first among preferred electrification/data-centre stocks after the sell-off. TP +57.6% vs spot.
Schneider Electric (SU FP) Dec26 call spread. UBS Research sees double-digit order growth in power grids and secure power infrastructure.
Air Liquide (AI FP) Dec26 call spread. Investment backlog hit a record EUR6bn and Q2 electronics sales grew 13.5% organically on AI-related semiconductor demand.
Anglo American (AAL LN) Dec26 call-spread collar. UBS Research calls it one of the cleanest expressions of mining's role in industrial capacity expansion.
YOFC (6869 HK) put-selling. Buy rated with target +196% above spot. Earnings case rests on supply constraints.
Kingboard Laminates (1888 HK) put-selling. Buy rated with target +86% above spot. Earnings case rests on supply constraints.

earnings_insights: Schedule noted in the screens: Santander (SAN SQ) and SSAB report 28-Oct, Credit Agricole and CaixaBank 30-Oct, Shell 29-Oct, Eli Lilly, Starbucks, Caterpillar, TAL Edu 29-Oct, Exxon, Chevron and Berkshire 30-Oct.

Next earnings dates listed in the sell-screen include Kering 8-Feb, Safran 9-Feb, Adyen 10-Feb, Boeing 27-Oct (already reported at publication), UPS 27-Oct, HSBC 27-Oct, Booking 3-Nov, Sea 9-Nov and Alibaba 23-Nov.

Air Liquide Q2 electronics sales grew 13.5% organically on AI-related semiconductor demand, and its investment backlog reached a record EUR6bn with electronics at 40% of it (as quoted from UBS Research).
